title: Admission and application
description: Willing to apply to the Master in Public Management and Policy (PMP)? Discover if your Bachelor's Degree makes you eligible and apply today.

blocks.html:
Candidates who fulfil the academic and language requirements are invited to submit their application using the online form available on the page www.usi.ch/en/education-application.

In order to be admitted to the Master's degree in Public Management and Policy, candidates must have completed a Bachelor’s degree in public economics, business management, politics, sociology, law, communication sciences, or an equivalent university degree granted by a recognised university (see below the section "Recognised degrees").

It is also reminded that the Master in Public Management and Policy, being part of the SPAN - Swiss Public Administration Network and offered in partnership with the Universities of Lausanne and Bern, has its own regulations.

Selection and outcome

USI Master in Public Management and Policy candidates usually receive the outcome of their application within 20 working days from the day they submitted their application.
This deadline may vary; we would ask candidates to follow the instructions they receive once they have submitted their application.
Please note that, in case of missing or incomplete documents, the review process may take longer.

Good practice: navigate all the sections and the FAQ to discover everything you need to know about this programme.

items.title: Recognised degrees
items.html:
Admission to USI Master's programmes requires a Bachelor's degree from a university or another Swiss academic institution, or a foreign Bachelor's degree from an equivalent institution that is recognised or accredited in the country of origin.

The following requirements particularly apply:

  • The certificate must be awarded by a higher education institution recognised in the country where the applicant pursued their studies;
  • The university degree must confirm a programme of study lasting at least three years (minimum 180 ECTS credits);
  • At least 80% of the credits were earned at recognised higher education institutions;
  • At least 50% of the credits were earned at the university awarding the degree.

The Bachelor's degree must be completed prior to starting the Master's programme.
For further information visit the Section “Conditional Admission”.

University of Applied Sciences

Candidates with a Bachelor's degree from a University of Applied sciences may be admitted with an additional requirement of max 60 ECTS to be earned:

Candidates with a Bachelor's degree from a recognised University of Applied Sciences may be admitted with an additional requirement of max 60 ECTS to be earned during or before the beginning of the programme, with Bachelor or Master courses according to a study programme defined by the scientific director.
The terms and conditions of additional ECTS are decided on a case-by-case basis and communicated to the candidate once admission has been granted.

items.title: Language
items.html:
Core courses (1st year) are taught in Italian and English, and courses of the Public Policy and Sustainability specialization (2nd year) are taught in English.
Language certificates are not required.

Università della Svizzera italiana offers free language courses in Italian, English, French and German, further information can be found here.

items.title: Required documents for the application
items.html:
To complete their application, applicants are invited to submit the following documents through the online application form available at www.usi.ch/en/education-application:

  • Copy of a personal identity document (ID or passport)
  • Copies of academic qualifications* (Bachelor's degree / License, Master's degree, High School Diploma / school attendance certificate)
  • Certificate of Bachelor's / Master's exams (transcript)
  • Curriculum vitae (in the language of instruction of the programme)
  • Candidate's motivational letter (in the language of instruction of the programme)
  • Italian/ English language certificate (as specified in the "Language requirements" section)
  • Certified translation of diplomas not issued in Italian, German, French, English, or Spanish
  • Copy of the residence permit for foreign candidates already residing in Switzerland
  • Any additional documentation required by the form

* while awaiting the degree, the student must provide the transcript of exams taken, specifying in the application form the expected graduation date.

Candidates may apply for a maximum of two programmes. For each programme you apply for, a separated motivation letter must be uploaded.

items.title: Conditional admission
items.html:
If your university degree is still in progress, you may be granted conditional admission. The admission condition will be lifted upon submission of your final diploma, official transcripts, or equivalent documents.

Applicants are required to have completed all examinations, including any internships or practical training, before the beginning of the semester. If a thesis is required, it may be discussed at a later date, provided that the Bachelor's degree is successfully obtained no later than mid-December. Please note that conditional admission, allowing the thesis to be defended at a later stage, is limited to entry into the Autumn semester and is not applicable to candidates requiring a visa.

The specific deadlines and all further details regarding the submission of your final documents will be clearly indicated in your official admission letter.

items.title: Application fee
items.html:
Following cases are exempted from the application fee payment:

  • candidates with previous degree studies completed in countries signatories of the Lisbon Convention*

For those who are not exempted (see above), at the time of submission of the application form, a registration fee of CHF 100.- is required (application fee waiver is not possible).
The registration fee is non-refundable in the event of withdrawal by the student or rejection. In case of enrolment, the fee will be deducted from the first semester's tuition fees.

Payment methods

The payment through Saferpay is requested before submitting the application.
The application fee is non-refundable in the event of withdrawal by the student or rejection. In the event of enrolment, the fee will be deducted from the first semester's tuition fees.

*What is the Lisbon Convention?

The Lisbon Convention regulates the recognition of university degrees between signatory countries and considerably simplifies the administration of admission procedures.
For this reason, candidates whose previous degree studies were completed in countries inside this Convention (see list below), are exempted from the application fee.

items.title: Fraud warning / Security notice
items.html:
In order to better protect future USI students against potential fraud, we wish to draw attention to fake USI intermediary services and/or misleading advertisements on the Internet, as well as related board and accommodation/matriculation proposals.

USI has no intermediaries whatsoever in these roles.

Enrollment at USI can only occur when applications are validated by its Faculty admission officers or when submitted online - in Italian or in English - via the official website of USI. The latter offers all relevant information on admission requirements, procedures, fees and accommodation: www.usi.ch/en.

When in doubt, we strongly recommend:

  • To check and verify the identity of the intermediary;
  • Not to submit any personal documents or information;
  • To pay particular attention to messages written in languages other than Italian or English, which are the only two languages used by USI for all its official communications;
  • To be suspicious of any advance payment requests, as USI does not request advance payment of tuition fees and/or rent.

Please report any fake or fraudulent advertisements to USI: info@usi.ch.

USI shall take no responsibility for damages relating to incidents of this kind, to the use of such intermediary services, and to the acceptance of such proposals.
